title: Twisted-arrow graph comparison is coinitial
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, mapping spaces, coherent functor categories and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the twisted-arrow construction $\operatorname{Tw}$ and its projection $\lambda$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration], and classification of left fibrations by space-valued coherent functors of [lem-coef-space-valued-straightening]. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor of quasicategories in a common sufficiently large universe $\mathcal V$. Define the simplicial pullback
$$W_f=(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A)\times_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal B),$$
using $1\times f$ on the first factor and $\lambda$ on the second. Its projection to $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A$ is the left fibration classified by the coherent mapping-space functor $(x,a)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,f(a))$, with the latter formed in the infinity category of $\mathcal V$-small spaces, in a larger ambient universe. The simplicial map
$$\kappa_f:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow W_f$$
is induced by $(f^{\mathrm{op}}\times1)\lambda$ and $\operatorname{Tw}(f)$; at an arrow $a\to a'$ it is the triple $(f(a),a',f(a\to a'))$. Its opposite $\kappa_f^{\mathrm{op}}$ is final: in every containing target universe, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, diagram $p:W_f^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ and $e\in\mathcal E$, restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(W_f^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta e)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)}(p\kappa_f^{\mathrm{op}},\Delta e).$$
Thus any specified cocone on $p$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction is colimiting, with the same vertex. The pullback, classification and graph map are natural in commutative squares of functors $f$. In particular, if $\mathcal A$ is $\mathcal U$-small for a smaller universe $\mathcal U$, the domain $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $\mathcal U$-small, even if $\mathcal B$ is not.

source.place: Proposition 5.6.9, its second canonical map (5.6.8.2), printed pp. 241-242; the mapping-space classifier is Section 5.6, Propositions 5.6.2, 5.6.5 and Remark 5.6.15, printed pp. 238-244. Definition 4.4.13, printed p. 160, calls a map cofinal when its opposite is final. The cocone-space formulation is Theorem 6.4.5, printed pp. 296-297. This variance convention is essential. Read online, July 30 2026 revision; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $T_B=\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal B)$ and $T_A=\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)$. The two projections $\lambda_B$ and $\lambda_A$ are left fibrations by [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Form $W_f$ degreewise as in the statement. A horn lifting problem for its projection to $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A$ projects to one for $\lambda_B$; a lift there, paired with the prescribed base simplex, is a lift in the pullback. Thus this projection is a left fibration. Opposites of quasicategories fill inner horns by reversing their indices; products fill them coordinatewise. A left fibration over such a base has a quasicategorical total space: fill the base inner horn and then lift it. This verifies the quasicategory hypotheses for both total spaces used below.

source.place: Proposition 5.6.2 and diagram (5.6.8.2); pullback lifting argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-space-valued-straightening] to $\lambda_B$ over the $\mathcal V$-small base $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B$. Its classifier is a coherent functor $H_B$ into $\mathcal V$-small spaces, constructed in a containing universe. Here is its mapping-space identification, rather than an inference from a mere agreement of vertex sets. For each target $y$, the natural second-block-collapse equivalence of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration] identifies the target-fixed part of $T_B$ with $(\mathcal B_{/y})^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. The transport comparison in [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit] identifies the right-fibration transport of $\mathcal B_{/y}$ with $x\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,y)$, coherently in $x$, with precomposition as its action. Taking opposites gives precisely the left-fibration transport over $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. For the remaining variable, a simplex of $T_B$ is a map on $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]$. Restricting it to the ordered vertices $\bar 1,\bar 0,0,1$ gives the commuting square taking an arrow $u:x\to y$ to $\beta u\alpha:x'\to y'$ over $(\alpha:x'\to x,\beta:y\to y')$. Every higher compatibility is restriction of the same join simplex; these restrictions commute with every $\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta$. Thus the classifier supplies the coherent precomposition/postcomposition mapping functor, not only separate bijections on components. Its value at $(x,y)$ is the right-pinched mapping space as a space, by the displayed slice transport comparison. Finally naturality of straightening under base pullback identifies the classifier of $W_f$ with $H_B(1\times f)$, namely $(x,a)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,f(a))$.

source.place: Propositions 5.6.5, 5.6.13, Corollary 5.6.14 and Remark 5.6.15; classification and its base-pullback compatibility

proof.text: For $\sigma:N([n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n])\to\mathcal A$, write $\sigma_-$ and $\sigma_+$ for its first- and second-block restrictions. Send it to the pullback simplex $((f\sigma_-,\sigma_+),f\sigma)$. Its two images in $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B$ are both $(f\sigma_-,f\sigma_+)$, so it lies in $W_f$. Restriction to a join operator commutes with postcomposition by $f$, hence this formula defines the simplicial map $\kappa_f$. At $n=0$ it gives exactly $(f(a),a',f(a\to a'))$.

source.place: Diagram (5.6.8.2), explicit formula for its canonical map

proof.text: To apply fiberwise coinitiality, swap the two base factors. Take $Z=\mathcal A$, $C=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$, $D=\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, $g=f^{\mathrm{op}}$, $X=T_A$, $Y=W_f$. Their maps to $Z\times C$ and $Z\times D$ are the left fibrations of Step 1 followed by the coordinate-swap isomorphisms. The formula of Step 3 gives $qh=(1_Z\times g)p$ for $h=\kappa_f$. At a vertex $a\in Z$, the fibers are $X_a=T_A\times_{\mathcal A}\{a\}$ and $Y_a=T_B\times_{\mathcal B}\{f(a)\}$. The latter equality follows degreewise: the second coordinate of a simplex in $\{a\}$ is constant at $a$, so its image under $f$ is constant at $f(a)$. These fibers are quasicategories since they are pullbacks of left fibrations to $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.6.9, second square, and Lemma 5.6.7 after interchanging product factors

proof.text: The target-fixed equivalences of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration] give, after taking opposites, equivalences $\mathcal A_{/a}\simeq X_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal B_{/f(a)}\simeq Y_a^{\mathrm{op}}$. By their naturality these intertwine $f$ on join slices with $h_a^{\mathrm{op}}$. They take the identity arrows to the identity-arrow vertices. Each identity edge is an equivalence (its inverse and both inverse triangles are degenerate), so [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] makes it final in the corresponding join slice. Equivalences preserve these final objects: a quasi-inverse supplies a preimage of every test object, and the mapping-space equivalences of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identify the relevant spaces with the contractible slice mapping spaces. Thus $X_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $Y_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ have final objects $t_a,t'_a$ given by the identity-arrow vertices, and $h_a^{\mathrm{op}}(t_a)=t'_a$ exactly. Taking opposites of a functor equivalence here is legitimate directly from its quasi-inverse and the two inverse natural equivalences.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.6.9: preservation of initial objects in the second square; Proposition 4.3.3; use opposites to keep the final-object convention

proof.text: Fix any target quasicategory $E$, diagram $F:Y_a^{\mathrm{op}}\to E$ and object $e$. By [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit], $F(t'_a)$ is a colimit of $F$, with a cocone whose component at $t'_a$ is the identity; likewise $F(h_a^{\mathrm{op}}(t_a))=F(t'_a)$ is a colimit of $Fh_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ with identity component at $t_a$. The dual mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore says that evaluation at these vertices identifies both cocone spaces with $\operatorname{Map}_E(F(t'_a),e)$. Explicitly, the universal comparison sends $v:F(t'_a)\to e$ to its composite with the normalized colimit cocone, and evaluation sends it back to $v$; hence evaluation is its inverse equivalence. Restriction along $h_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ commutes with evaluation because $h_a^{\mathrm{op}}(t_a)=t'_a$. Its induced comparison is consequently an equivalence. This proves the fiber hypothesis for every target and every diagram, without any completeness assumption on $E$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3 / Corollary 6.4.6, normalized final-object colimits and their cocone-space characterization

proof.text: All the hypotheses of [lem-coef-left-fibration-fiberwise-coinitiality] are now verified: Step 4 gives the required left fibrations over products and the strictly commuting square; Step 6 proves its fiber hypothesis. Apply it to $h=\kappa_f$. Its conclusion is exactly the restriction equivalence displayed in the item for arbitrary $p:W_f^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ and $e\in\mathcal E$. This proves finality of $\kappa_f^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the required strong sense. The fixed size universe for this application is $\mathcal V$, not the potentially smaller universe in which $\mathcal A$ alone is small; any chosen target fits in a further containing universe.

source.place: Lemma 5.6.7 applied in the proof of Proposition 5.6.9, second canonical map; cocone-space formulation of finality

proof.text: For a specified cocone $c:p\to\Delta L$ and every test object $e$, form the square whose upper row is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L,e)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(W_f^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta e)$ induced by $c$ and whose lower row is the analogous map induced by its restriction. The left vertical map is the identity and the right vertical map is the restriction equivalence of Step 7; the square commutes by composition of coherent transformations. Thus one horizontal map is an equivalence if and only if the other is. The cocone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that $c$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction is, with exactly the same vertex $L$.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.5, specified-cocone consequence via the mapping-space criterion

proof.text: For a strictly commutative square $vf=f'u$ with $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ and $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$, the pullback map sends $((x,a),\tau)$ to $((v(x),u(a)),v\tau)$. The defining equalities for its image follow from $vf=f'u$. On a join simplex $\sigma$ the two composites with the graph maps are both $((vf\sigma_-,u\sigma_+),vf\sigma)$, so naturality of $\kappa$ is strict. The map of left fibrations factors through the pullback of $W_{f\prime}$ along $v^{\mathrm{op}}\times u$. Straightening takes this map over the common base to a coherent transformation, and its naturality under base pullback identifies the target classifier with the restriction of the classifier of $W_{f\prime}$. The block-collapse maps commute with postcomposition, so this transformation is the mapping-space map induced by $v$, including its higher coherences. Finally, if $\mathcal A$ is $\mathcal U$-small, then in each degree $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)_n$ is identified with $\mathcal A_{2n+1}$ by the order isomorphism $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]\cong[2n+1]$. Thus it is $\mathcal U$-small; the opposite changes only its simplicial operators, not its degreewise sets. No size bound on $\mathcal B$ in $\mathcal U$ was used.

source.place: Paragraph 5.6.8, functoriality of the canonical maps, and definition (5.6.1.3), degreewise size
